answer:
Chandrayaan-3 produced multiple scientific findings rather than one single key result.

Scientists from NRSC/ISRO estimate that about 2.06 tonnes of lunar epiregolith were ejected and displaced over an area of 108.4 m2 around the landing site [1]. LIBS confirmed the presence of Sulphur on the lunar surface through unambiguous in-situ measurements [1]. The "Hop" experiment revealed regolith heterogeneity at the Moon's south pole [3]. This study marks the first of such class of unique measurements [3]. Scientists from PRL and ISRO showed that the mission landed within a buried impact crater around 160 km in size [5]. The same study described the crater as roughly 4.4 km deep [5]. It is likely to be older than the South Pole Aitken basin [5].
